The Wgpu documentation follows the [Diátaxis](https://diataxis.fr/) structure: four sections, one for each thing a reader comes for, and a fifth for working on the module itself.

{{< cards >}}
  {{< card link="tutorials/" title="Tutorials" subtitle="Seven chapters in order, from installing the module through buffers, compute shaders, shader checks and textures to drawing, commands and tasks." icon="academic-cap" >}}
  {{< card link="how-to/" title="How-to" subtitle="One task each: choose an adapter, count a histogram on the GPU, keep a simulation's data there, prepare textures for a renderer, chart data into images, and more." icon="book-open" >}}
  {{< card link="reference/" title="Reference" subtitle="Every task with its examples, every cmdlet's syntax and parameters, every class and enumeration, every error id, and where it has been run." icon="document-text" >}}
  {{< card link="explanation/" title="Explanation" subtitle="Why the module exists, what it keeps while it is loaded, how data moves, and which graphics APIs it reaches where." icon="light-bulb" >}}
  {{< card link="building/" title="Building From Source" subtitle="Build the module, test a change, and update these pages." icon="code" >}}
{{< /cards >}}
